newsitem.title: USA: U.S. nuclear regulator to announce reorganization.
newsitem.headline: U.S. nuclear regulator to announce reorganization.

text.p: U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission chairwoman Shirley Jackson is set to announce a "major reorganization" of the agency next Monday, an NRC spokesman said Wednesday.
The NRC would not comment on what kinds of changes were in store.
The commission has come under heavy criticism in the last year for failing to do its job.
At an oversight hearing last September, House lawmakers attacked the federal regulators for allowing safety lapses at nuclear plants to go unchecked for many years.

A spokesman for the Nuclear Energy Institute, which represents utilities with nuclear plants, would not speculate on the NRC's reorganization, but said the industry had "always supported ... the collegial approach of the commission."
Anti-nuclear groups have long attacked the "collegial approach", saying top NRC staff were too cozy with the industry.
"If (the reorganization) involves shaking up the old guard in higher level staff positions at the NRC, that would certainly be a good step," said Bill Magavern of consumer group Public Citizen.

"Senior staff have been frustrating the aims both of Chairwoman Jackson and of the plant level staff, resident inspectors, when it comes to actually making utilities comply with safety rules," said Magavern.
He pointed to the recent "abrupt" resignation of the director of the NRC's office of nuclear reactor regulation, William Russell, a 20-year veteran of the agency, as an example of positive change.
An NRC spokeswoman said he quit the agency for "personal reasons".
Critics of the agency have said Jackson, who was appointed last year, has been moving in the right direction to tighten enforcement of the agency's safety rules.
Earlier this year, after serious safety problems at Northeast Utilities' Millstone nuclear plant in Connecticut raised a public outcry, the NRC forced the plant to shut down all three of its units.
